characterList.description: Male, grey hair, mustache, wearing glasses, a plaid shirt, and a black vest. He is sitting in a room with a beige wall and a decorative sculpture visible behind him.
characterList.name: Salih Mislim

content_metadata.description: An interview with Salih Mislim by a VOA journalist, discussing Turkish actions and the Kurdish situation in Syria.

qAndA.answer: The label "skype" beneath his name indicates a remote connection.
qAndA.question: What visual cue suggests Salih Mislim is participating remotely?

qAndA.answer: His calm demeanor suggests a lack of fear or surprise, implying he believes the charges are politically motivated and holds confidence in his position.
qAndA.question: What does Salih Mislim's reaction to the arrest warrant reveal about his attitude?

qAndA.answer: He argues Turkey is not genuinely fighting ISIS but using the conflict to target the Kurds and further its own political agenda.
qAndA.question: What is Salih Mislim's main criticism of Turkey's actions in Syria?

qAndA.answer: He accuses Turkey of using "blackmailing" tactics to pressure Western nations on issues like refugees and economic ties.
qAndA.question: How does Salih Mislim characterize Turkey's diplomatic approach?

qAndA.answer: He seeks strengthened diplomatic and political relations, hoping the new administration will engage with the Kurdish perspective on the situation in Syria.
qAndA.question: What does Salih Mislim hope for from the new US administration?

characterInteraction.description: The interviewer is direct and asks pointed questions, while Salih Mislim provides measured and thoughtful answers. There is a sense of mutual respect despite differing viewpoints.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Salih Mislim's calm demeanor in the face of the arrest warrant may suggest confidence in his position and a belief that Turkey's actions are politically motivated. His consistent emphasis on peaceful co-existence with other Kurdish parties implies a desire for unity within the Kurdish community. His criticism of Turkey's involvement in Syria highlights the complex geopolitical dynamics and conflicting interests at play in the region.

mood.description: Neutral - The split screen format and professional attire of both characters create a neutral and informative atmosphere. The interview is conducted in a calm and respectful manner, further contributing to the overall content mood.

narrativeProgression.description: Introduction of Salih Mislim and the arrest warrant issued by Turkey.
Salih Mislim's initial reaction to the arrest warrant.
Discussion about Turkey's claims of organic links between PYD and PKK.
Salih Mislim's stance on PYD's relationship with PKK.

What is Turkey trying to do? How do you comment this move from Ankara?
Well, it's not the first time they are saying so, but it's the first time I mean,
is one arrest from the court, I mean, in Ankara, which is totally false. I mean, even if you remember this
everybody, incident, what happened, I mean, we condemned it, it was okay. And then
TAK said, over responsibility for it, it was okay. I mean, nobody said that you are related.
And at that time they mentioned the name from Amodar, we searched if there was nobody under
this name or from all Amodar. So it's nothing to do. And secondly, I am not a Turkish citizen,
I mean, I don't know if you want to check it. So now it will be a fact I don't know, really.
But well, we wouldn't do anything for us. Maybe the, their aim is just to prevent our
moving in Europe and talking to the politicians and the governments and peace in Europe. And so
I think it wouldn't have been from our side, it wouldn't have been.
So the aim of this move is to restrict, to limit your diplomatic affairs, diplomatic work in Europe,
but you don't think it's going to be effective? And no, I don't think so, because well,
there is nobody will be, will take care of this, I mean, it's such a resolution also.
Because everybody knows there is no, I mean, there is no, nothing true, I mean, behind this,
what they have said, yes.
Turkey has long been saying that PYD and PKK have organic links. And how do you comment on that?
What is your relationship with the PKK?
One, we respect all the Pakistani parties and they were from our side in the dark days and still,
we see them helpful. We would like to have a good relationship with all the party and all the
same for us. PKK and PUK and Islamists and even HDP and PKK is one of those party,
not parties. And other parties, I mean, are sharing the same people. And so it's all right.
But for organic relations, we don't have any organic relations. If they want, maybe they can't
sign any agreement with us and to see if we are going to PKK or not. And they're not better
than everybody that we are independent for our decisions. We are decided for Roger. I'm going to keep
doing so. Coming back to Lajaba, there are reports that in the Baban-Membjj area, Turkish attacks
has been intensified in recent days. How is this affecting the global war against ISIS? Whereas
the such an important operation to liberate Raka has started, is this hindering the efforts of
Kurds and their allies to liberate Raka? The Turkish recent moves.
Well, sure. I mean, from the beginning, we said Turkey is helping ISIS, not going to fight against
ISIS anytime because it's a tool used by Turkey against the Kurds. And maybe they have created
this tool even. And because of that, we don't think there will be any serious fighting between
Turkish side and for. And we saw this example in general, this one, they moved in. There were
some times, remember, they just had their build and changed their clothes, they became a soldier of
Turkey, decided to be society fighting. So because of that, I think the Turkish invasion to see
and actifying the land is just helpful and die. And just to remember, I mean, it came when they
were preparing to start the liberation of Raka. So they made this invasion. It's still insisting
by doing so, trying to prevent any defeat of damage by this health and this movement.
And now, even in the villages active by Turkey, there is no difference between them and Dasha.
They are changing the demography for the areas, the villages. We're moving the first,
the same old Dasha was doing, they are continuing like with it. So of course, I mean, it will affect
our efforts internationally because Turkey is not genuine for fighting Dasha. They are
on the same, you know, multiple and they said we will share it and we will do it in Bashi,
Kansol. So they didn't allow them. We hope they will allow Turkey here also.
Why is the world silent? If you're what you're saying is true, how come the international community
is silent not doing anything to prevent this? Well, I think because Turkey's diplomacy, especially
against the world, and Europe is depending on the Blackmailing, they are trying to
Blackmail for everything and even for refugees, for injuredly, for fighting also. So they are Blackmailing
so I mean, it's threat by Turkey themselves to them to cut the relations. I mean, maybe
economic relations and the economy for guys and changing them from Europe to Russia and so
for their clients. I think this is for the problem as you shouldn't be like that. Mr. Muslim,
my last question about the new president of the United States, Mr. Donald Trump is going to be
the new president of the United States. How do you predict, how do you foresee the relationship between
the Syrian Kurds and the new US administration, especially the war against ISIS and also do you
expect this relationship to gain political and social and economic aspects as well?
Well, I think the strategy of the big country like the United States, big power, it wouldn't be
changed by changing the president because this strategy at least, what I know, it was planned since
2001. But it wouldn't be changed so easily. It could be harder or softer is something different,
I mean, depending on that. But what we are expecting, I mean, this hard line will continue against
terrorism and these are lines between the democratic Syrian forces and the international
allies will be strengthened what we are expecting. Yes. And of course, I mean from our side,
maybe we have allies against ISIS till now, for fighting in the army side only. Of course,
we are expecting to have diplomatic relations and political relations, at least to listen to us
to understand what we are doing. We are expecting such from the new administration also, I mean,
to have good and close relations, politically evenness. Mr. Muslim, thank you very much for speaking
to the O.A. Thank you.
